details.description: DeepSeek-Coder-1.3B-Base is a 1.3-billion-parameter code-focused language model from DeepSeek AI, trained on 1 trillion tokens (the DeepSeek Coder family overall was trained on a 2-trillion-token corpus, 87% code and 13% natural language in English and Chinese) with a 16K-token context window. It is part of the DeepSeek Coder family (1.3B, 5.7B, 6.7B and 33B sizes) built for project-level code completion and fill-in-the-middle infilling. This is the base checkpoint, not an instruction-tuned chat model.
advantages: Supports project-level code completion and fill-in-the-blank (infilling) tasks across a repository, per DeepSeek's model card.
Pretrained on 1 trillion tokens spanning code and natural language in both English and Chinese, per DeepSeek's model card.
DeepSeek's model license supports commercial use.
disadvantages: This is a base checkpoint, not instruction-tuned, so it is built for code completion and infilling rather than following chat instructions.
DeepSeek's model card names the benchmarks it was tested on (HumanEval, MultiPL-E, MBPP, DS-1000, APPS) but does not publish numeric scores for this specific 1.3B size.
use_cases: Code completion within a single file or across a repository.
As a base checkpoint for further fine-tuning into a coding assistant.

notes: Catalog facts list max tokens as 16384 (16K), matching the model card's 16K context window, so kept as-is. No numeric benchmark scores are published on the model card for this specific 1.3B size, only benchmark names, so evaluations is left empty. This is a base (non-instruction-tuned) checkpoint despite the catalog's 'chat' kind; flagging since users choosing it for chat/instruction use should know it is not RLHF/instruct-tuned. The model card page mixes two token counts: its generic family intro says every size is 'trained from scratch on 2T tokens,' but its model-specific 'Model Summary' section states plainly 'deepseek-coder-1.3b-base is a 1.3B parameter model with Multi-Head Attention trained on 1 trillion tokens.' Corrected description/advantages to the model-specific 1T figure and noted the family-wide 2T figure separately, since the family-wide 2T total (1.8T pretrain + 0.2T context extension per the GitHub README) applies to the larger checkpoints, not confirmed for the 1.3B.
